newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Swire Pacific likely to post steady profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Swire Pacific likely to post steady profit growth.

text.p: Hong Kong conglomerate Swire Pacific Ltd is expected to report solid profit growth this week of 13 percent to 14 percent, analysts said.
Janice Wallace, who follows the company for Goldman Sachs (Asia), said she forecast attributable profits of HK$7.37 billion ($945 million) for the year and earnings per share (EPS) of HK$4.64.
This represents an increase of 14.2 percent for Swire's 1995 net profits, and a 14 percent increase in EPS.
The consensus forecast in the Estimate Directory is for attributable profits of HK$7.282 billion for the year to December, up 12.8 percent compared to 1995.
Last year, Swire reported a 16 percent increase in attributable profits year-on-year.

Swire, with roots stretching back to the founding of the British colony, has interests spanning aviation, property, industries, trading, marine services and insurance and insurance but the glamorous aviation sector is taking a back seat to property.
SBC Warburg said it was forecasting HK$7.339 billion in attributable earnings, a rise of 13.7 percent, and an EPS of HK$4.63.
Dogged by concerns over Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd, Swire's share underperformed the market in late 1996, but it has attracted more attention this year.
Swire last April, restructured its aviation interests.

It pruned its Cathay Pacific stake from 52.6 percent to 43.86 percent in a complex deal that saw mainland-controlled CITIC Pacific Ltd more than double its stake in the airline to 25 percent from 10 percent.

In a related deal, state-owned China National Aviation Corp said it would buy into Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd, acquiring a 17.66 percent from Swire and Cathay Pacific, which had controlled the airline, and 17.66 percent from CITIC Pacific.
In January, Swire was one of 119 stocks from around the world that Salomon Brothers singled out as likely to perform well in 1997.
Despite the concerns over Cathay Pacific's prospects, aviation was of diminishing importance to Swire, analysts said.
Salomon Brothers has predicted that Cathay Pacific's contribution to Swire's pre-tax profits would fall to just 17 percent in 1997.
Wallace said Cathay Pacific's performance had been fairly flat last year while the rest of Swire had been growing "at a reasonable clip."
"We would be looking for a pretty reasonable contribution from the property side," Wallace said.
SBC Warburg predicted that Swire would be the territory's largest listed landlord in Hong Kong by 1998.

Morgan Stanley also said in a report on the Hong Kong property sector earlier this year that Swire had made the transition from being a developer of residential property for sale "to more of an investment property company".
But while Swire had an "excellent property portfolio" airline concerns were likely to continue to dominate sentiment, Morgan Stanley said.
Steven Thompson of Nikko Research Center said he was expecting attributable profits of HK$7.379 billion, up 14.33 percent compared with 1995. He expected an EPS of HK$4.65.
He expected property trading to contribute HK$1.658 billion in earnings before interest and tax, and money from property investment to rise eight percent to HK$3.313 billion.
Ky Ng of BZW Asia has forecast HK$7.132 billion for Swire in 1996, up 10.5 percent compared to 1995.
Analysts said that without exceptionals profits, growth in core operations in 1996 would be relatively flat.
